text:
incident-bot: Pager alert triggered: GPU prefill OOMs on runtime pool 'prefill-us-west-2' — multiple container restarts detected. Severity: P2.

sam: I'm on it, joining bridge. seeing repeated container restart loops on gpu-node-42.

jess: thanks — logs show OOM during large-context prefill (user payload ~1.2M tokens). stack: `RuntimePrefill::allocate_kv(+0x4a)` then `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`.

carlos: node metrics show VRAM steadily climbing before crash, kvcache growth spikes. no recent deploys in that pool.

sam: can we hot-swap traffic off that pool? start redirecting >90% of prefill to fallback pool with smaller model.

jess: doing canary redirect now: updating routing policy to prefer 'prefill-fallback' for requests with context > 512k tokens.

deploy-bot: routing update: policy `prefill-large-context` -> target `prefill-fallback` (activated by sam).

maria: any customer impact yet? which tenants hit this?

sam: early list: acme-analytics, beta-chat, and a handful of enterprise test tenants. some 429s and increased latency reported.

ashley: I'm drafting a short customer note: "We're mitigating an OOM in GPU prefill for very large contexts; we routed affected requests to fallback infra and are investigating root cause. No data loss." Want review.

jess: good. also running `kubectl logs -f prefill-runtime-xyz` — attaching snippet: ```oom-kernel: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
Stack: allocate_kv -> prefill_worker -> request_handler```

carlos: temp mitigation: enable aggressive kvcache trimming on prefills (>64k tokens) and cap prefill length at 1M tokens for the pool. I'll roll that patch to the runtime config.

sam: please also cordon gpu-node-42 for deeper inspection after we stabilize.

maria: customer note ready, I posted to #customer-ops draft channel, will send once we confirm fallback routing is stable.

jess: applying kvcache trim now (config flag `kvcache.trim_threshold=65536`). patch deployed to prefill pool.

carlos: node cordoned and restart of runtime process scheduled at +5m to capture coredump.

sam: monitoring — error rate dropping, restart loops stopped on node-42. fallback pool handling heavy prefill traffic but within SLA for most tenants.

maria: sending initial notification to affected customers now. message: "We've routed large-context requests to a fallback model while we investigate GPU OOMs; some requests may see slightly lower throughput. We'll follow up with root cause."

jess: collecting heap/KV dump; saving to /mnt/diag/prefill-1876543211.tar.gz.

carlos: ops checklist: 1) cordon node (done), 2) collect coredump (scheduled), 3) capture kvcache dump (done), 4) increase alert threshold to catch early VRAM growth.

sam: assigning follow-ups: jess -> runtime trace + repro; carlos -> node-level memory analysis; ashley -> postmortem owner; maria -> customer follow-up.

ashley: I have a slot for a short incident scrub at 09:00 PT tomorrow. I'll create calendar invite.

jess: initial hypothesis: large contiguous KV allocations + a corner-case leak during prefill blocking async eviction -> OOM + illegal mem access on the GPU driver. will try to reproduce locally with synthetic long-context prefills.

carlos: if we confirm a leak, plan is: backport kvcache bounds, add async eviction throttle, and ship a runtime patch.

sam: OK good work team. For now, keep fallback routing in place until we have tested a patch and proven node stability for 24h.

incident-bot: Incident P2 acknowledged by sam, bridge closed at 1876543333 (mitigations active, customer notifications sent).
